key_insight: This paper shows that LLMs can be improved with reinforcement learning even when no ground-truth answers exist, by using ranking-based, deterministic execution feedback as a training signal. In short, the model learns from relative quality scores instead of exact solutions.
problem_solved: Traditional RL with verifiable rewards depends on known ground-truth answers, which limits it to tasks where exact solutions are available. This paper addresses how to train LLMs on score-based optimization tasks where the correct answer is unknown or hard to define.
method: Introduces RiVER (Ranking-induced VERifiable framework) to convert deterministic execution feedback into continuous-valued supervision.
Uses group-relative reinforcement learning to compare outputs and optimize ranking-based rewards instead of requiring exact labels.
Applies the framework to tasks with score-based objectives, enabling learning from verifiable signals even without ground-truth solutions.
impact: This broadens the set of real-world tasks where RL can be used to improve LLMs, including problems with ambiguous or unknown target answers. For practitioners, it offers a practical path to train models on execution traces, scores, or other deterministic feedback signals instead of expensive labeled solutions.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing input prompt -> model outputs -> execution feedback -> ranking-based reward -> updated LLM.
A side-by-side comparison chart of traditional RLVR vs. RiVER (ground-truth required vs. no ground-truth required).
An illustration of ranking scores or a leaderboard-style output ordering multiple candidate responses.
Icons representing deterministic execution, continuous reward signals, and reinforcement learning loops.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs
paper_authors: Yingyu Lin, Qiyue Gao, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Xunpeng Huang, Kun Zhou
